text: The binary is fully functional with no INTENT_HOME in the environment **and the variable is not read at all, which is stronger than an override and is deliberate** **PARENTHETICAL CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (vc), on dc's measurement, on a row that is already GREEN -- which is where a stale claim survives, because nothing re-examines a closed criterion (issue 0032, this contract's own weighing).** The row read _"demoted to dev override"_, and **there is no override: `$INTENT_HOME` is never read from the environment.** Measured by dc on one binary three ways -- set in the environment: `<not set>`; absent: `<not set>`; from inside an install: the real path -- and confirmed by vc at source, where **zero `var("INTENT_HOME")` or `var_os("INTENT_HOME")` calls exist in any crate.** `intent info` self-locates by walking up from its resolved executable path. **THE MAIN CLAUSE IS TRUE AND THE GREEN STANDS**; AT-11.3 proves the binary is fully functional without the variable. It is the parenthetical that described a mechanism which does not exist -- **and the danger of leaving it is that a reader implementing to the contract would build the override back, which is precisely what happened once already: the first version of `install.rs` built one, and ic's `no_intent_home.rs` refused it.** **THE REASON IT MUST NEVER EXIST, hoisted here out of `install.rs:20` where it has been living as a code comment (cc):** the assets are VERSIONED, and `lib/templates/.claude/scripts/` in a v2 install and a v3 install are **different files with the same names**. A machine mid-rollout has both trees and a `$INTENT_HOME` left over from v2, so an override would make the v3 binary exec **v2's hook scripts**, silently, from a variable the operator set years earlier for a different tool. **The environment cannot know which version is running; the executable's own location always does.** **THAT IS WHY THIS IS A CONTRACT EDIT AND NOT A COMMENT: a ratified reason living in a transcription is found only by whoever next touches that transcription (cc's own rule, third instance today), and the contract is what a builder reads first.** **AND THE FIXTURE THAT FOUND IT PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON FIRST:** dc's first attempt set the variable and PASSED, because `cargo test` puts the binary under `target/` inside the repository, so walking up found a tree with `lib/templates/` in it. **The variable was doing nothing and the LAYOUT was doing all of it.** It surfaced only under a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, which moved the build out of the tree -- the subject moving out from under the instrument, caught by moving it deliberately.
